original_value: The classification performance of passive sonar can be improved by extracting the features of ship-radiated noise. Traditional feature extraction methods neglect the nonlinear features in ship-radiated noise, such as entropy. The multiscale sample entropy (MSE) algorithm has been widely used for quantifying the entropy of a signal, but there are still some limitations. To remedy this, the hierarchical cosine similarity entropy (HCSE) is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the hierarchical decomposition is utilized to decompose a time series into some subsequences. Then, the sample entropy (SE) is modified by utilizing Shannon entropy rather than conditional entropy and employing angular distance instead of Chebyshev distance. Finally, the complexity of each subsequence is quantified by the modified SE. Simulation results show that the HCSE method overcomes some limitations in MSE. For example, undefined entropy is not likely to occur in HCSE, and it is more suitable for short time series. Compared with MSE, the experimental results illustrate that the classification accuracy of real ship-radiated noise is significantly improved from 75% to 95.63% by using HCSE. Consequently, the proposed HCSE can be applied in practical applications.

result.paraphrase: Passive sonar classification performance can be enhanced by extracting features from ship-radiated noise. Conventional feature extraction methods overlook nonlinear characteristics in such noise, including entropy. Although the multiscale sample entropy (MSE) algorithm is widely used to quantify signal entropy, it still has certain limitations. To address these issues, this paper proposes hierarchical cosine similarity entropy (HCSE). First, hierarchical decomposition is used to split a time series into several subsequences. Next, sample entropy (SE) is revised by replacing conditional entropy with Shannon entropy and substituting angular distance for Chebyshev distance. Finally, the complexity of each subsequence is measured using the modified SE. Simulation results indicate that HCSE overcomes some shortcomings of MSE; for instance, undefined entropy is less likely to occur, and it is better suited to short time series. Compared with MSE, experiments show that HCSE significantly improves real ship-radiated-noise classification accuracy from 75% to 95.63%. Therefore, the proposed HCSE is suitable for practical applications.
